newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes moderate losses, Jul/Aug roll wider.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes moderate losses, Jul/Aug roll wider.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf continued to track a weaker course Wednesday afternoon, but losses have been trimmed in half from late morning.

Outright prices remained at the mercy of headlines from the OPEC meeting in Vienna, and possible confirmation on when Iraq will resume lifting crude oil under the second round of the "oil-for-food" accord with the United Nations.

For the most part, outrights have sunk below the even level due to slightly bearish weekly inventory reports, leaving futures around five cents off at $18.95-19.05 a barrel for August NYMEX contracts. Cash benchmark August prices were also at those levels, but widened the advantage over July WTI to some 30-35 cents, traders said.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was pegged at $18.65-75 a barrel, 10 cents weaker than late Tuesday. After today's session, July business will be complete.
For the grades, August Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James held a 5-7 cents premium to the benchmark, with Midland/WTI around 30 cents under WTI/Cushing.
West Texas Sour/Midland was last talked at $1.35-45 under the August marker, with no fresh traded recorded.

Traders said August Exchange for Physicals were talked around four cents over the cash screen quotes. Last trades on the July/August roll were heard at -32 cents, down from the weaker -35/37 cents levels in the morning.
